subject: HealthZen: training block, subprocessor inventory and cross-border handling
messages:
From: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@healthzen.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Ross <procurement@healthzen.com>, legal@healthzen.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Preliminary DPA items — model improvement / training exclusion and subprocessors

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HealthZen is excited about the latency numbers. Before we progress to signature, our legal and procurement teams asked for clarification on two points in the DPA:

1) An explicit no-training (no-model-improvement) commitment for customer-provided prompts/responses (we've highlighted the clause in the attached redline). We need to understand how Redwood enforces this in hosted vs dedicated modes and what controls you provide to operationalize opt-outs.

2) A current subprocessor inventory and any planned transfers outside the US. We also need an evidence pack or path to produce logs showing that customer data was not used for model updates for a given timeframe.

I've attached HealthZen_DPA_redline_v3.pdf with inline comments. Can your team confirm what you can commit to and what evidence we can expect post-signature?

Thanks,
Jordan Fields
Corporate Counsel, HealthZen
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@healthzen.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary DPA items — model improvement / training exclusion and subprocessors

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear redline and the follow-up. Quick summary of what Redwood can offer and proposed next steps: 

- No-training commitment: We can agree to a contractual no-model-improvement commitment for customer data (prompts/responses) in the hosted API when the customer enables the "no-train" flag and for all Dedicated/Private deployments by default. Operationally we isolate and tag traffic at the routing layer; tagged requests are excluded from training pipelines and any offline datasets.

- Evidence & audit: Post-signature we can provide an evidence bundle consisting of: (a) subprocessor inventory snapshot, (b) routing logs showing the no-train tag flows (token-level hashes, not raw content), and (c) a signed operations attestation covering the applicable date range. For sensitive customers we support per-customer KV-cache purging hooks and token-level retention TTLs.

- Cross-border transfers: Our standard is to keep customer data in region where requested; hosted endpoints default to region pinned by the customer. For HealthZen (US primary), we can contractually restrict processing to US regions and list any subprocessors who may have EU or APAC infrastructure.

Proposed next steps:
1) Our legal & product ops will prepare the evidence template and an appendix describing the operational controls.
2) We suggest a short 30-min call this week with HealthZen legal to walk through what the evidence looks like in practice (routing logs + attestation).
3) If the redline is acceptable after the appendix, we'll prepare a signable DPA (DocuSign link).

I'm looping in Lauren (sales) to coordinate timeline and Grace (product) for the technical appendix.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@healthzen.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Ross <procurement@healthzen.com>, legal@healthzen.com
Date: 2026-10-28T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary DPA items — model improvement / training exclusion and subprocessors

Thanks Dev — that helps. Two follow-ups from our side: 

- Evidence: For the routing logs you mention, HealthZen will need a way to correlate a set of request IDs to the non-training flag without seeing customer content. Would token hashes + timestamps + request IDs be sufficient? We need the ability to validate a claim on demand (audit within 90 days).

- Subprocessors: please include any third parties used for observability (we've had concerns historically about telemetry services that ingest logs). The inventory and any contractual flow-down commitments are essential.

Ava — can we schedule the 30-min slot for Thursday 10/29 at 10am PT?

Jordan

Date: 2026-10-29T08:12:00-07:00

Jordan/Ava — call confirmed for Thu 10/29 10am PT. Joining: Dev, Grace, and Karthik for engineering/security detail.

Quick note from commercial — if you need a hard commitment on region residency for the duration of procurement (e.g., until contract renewal), we can add a geographic processing appendix. I'll also share the proposed commercial milestone schedule in the call so procurement can align.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop

Attachment: redline_comments_20261028.docx
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Fields <jordan.fields@healthzen.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Technical appendix & evidence artifacts for no-training commitment

Jordan — following our call, attaching the outline of the technical appendix we discussed. High-level points: 

- How no-train tagging works: request-level header + internal routing metadata; the flag is carried through the serving runtime and is excluded from any training dumps.
- Evidence bundle: (1) subprocessor_inventory_20261027.csv (snapshot), (2) sample routing log format (redacted) — includes request_id, timestamp, routing_tag, worker_id, model_variant, and hash(token_window) fields, (3) ops attestation template (signed by Redwood SOC/Ops).
- Retention & purge: documented TTLs and API endpoints for customer-initiated purge.

We cannot provide raw content as part of the audit; the evidence approach relies on deterministic hashes and signed attestation to prove the exclusion. If HealthZen requires full-request replay for forensic reasons, that would need a bespoke escrow arrangement (we can draft options).

Grace O'Connor
Product, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthZen DPA — next steps and signatures

Team —

Thanks for the appendix and the demo of the evidence format. Procurement reviewed the subprocessor inventory and had two asks before we sign: 

1) Add observability vendor names that receive log metadata (not content) and confirm whether any of those vendors have staff outside the US who might access telemetry.
2) Add a 90-day audit window clause and a clear contact for escalation if audits are requested.

If you can confirm both items we will circulate the redline internally and push to sign by EOD Monday. We will need the finalized DPA as a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Ava Ross
Head of Procurement, HealthZen

Subject: Re: HealthZen DPA — next steps and signatures

Ava/Jordan —

Summary update and actions: 
- Observability vendors: We will provide a vetted list of telemetry/observability subprocessors and note staffing locations. For standard hosted plans we use TelemetraOps (US/EU staff), MetricsFlow (US only), and our internal telemetry cluster (Redwood employees only). We will mark TelemetraOps and MetricsFlow on the subprocessor inventory with access notes.
- 90-day audit window: we accept a contractual 90-day audit window for the evidence bundle; audit requests route to security@redwood.ai and our SOC/Ops team will coordinate.

I've uploaded the final DPA to DocuSign and shared the link here: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/HZ-2026-117 — Jordan, if HealthZen legal is good, please sign and we'll trigger the evidence snapshot.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
